<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->
# seakarr

Automated Soulseek music downloader with library quality upgrading.

## Features

- **Library quality scanner** — walks your music library directories, reads audio tags (FLAC, MP3, AAC,
  OGG, Opus, WAV, WMA, and more via [lofty](https://crates.io/crates/lofty)), and identifies albums
  whose tracks are in a format outside `filters.allowed_extensions` or fall below the
  configurable bitrate threshold.
- **Upgrade mode** — for each album needing an upgrade, searches the Soulseek network, ranks
  candidates by advertised speed (adjusted by measured-throughput reputation), free-slot bonus, bitrate bonus,
  album-name match and peer reliability, and downloads the best match. The result is written into your
  library when the artist already has a folder under a configured `library.paths` entry, and stays in
  `storage.staging_dir` when it does not; an album selected by `library_upgrade.enabled` is replaced in
  place. An upgrade whose every destination already holds a strictly better file
  keeps those files and still completes the album, so the staging copy is removed without a new file being
  written. A candidate whose files omit the bitrate attribute scores zero on the bitrate bonus once
  `filters.min_bit_rate` is set, so a peer that reports one is preferred; it is still admitted, because its
  real quality is verified after download.
- **Discover mode** — derives the artist list from your library (tags first,
  folder names as the fallback), keeps only the artists that own a folder of
  their own, asks MusicBrainz which conceptual albums each of those is missing,
  and downloads only those. An artist the library only knows as a guest inside
  another artist's folder is skipped, and the run summary reports how many were
  skipped that way; name one explicitly with `--artist` to process it anyway.
  Naming an artist explicitly does not require the library to hold an album for
  it: when a folder named after the artist exists, the artist is processed and
  its albums are placed into that folder, and when there is neither an album nor
  a folder the run warns and keeps the downloads in staging.
  Albums already present are never
  searched or re-downloaded, and each run stops after
  `discover.max_cycle_downloads` download attempts so a large library fills in
  over successive runs. Release types come from `discography.allowed_types`.
- **Manual & batch modes** — search for a specific artist/album on demand, or process a newline-separated
  text file of `artist - album` lines to download a curated wantlist.
  A run places each completed album into the artist's existing library folder when one exists
  anywhere under a configured `library.paths` entry; when the artist has no folder there, or the
  album's destination folder already exists, a manual run keeps the download in
  `storage.staging_dir` (batch and upgrade runs merge into the existing folder instead, keeping
  any file that already parses as audio). An
  album-only request names no artist, so it always stays in staging and says nothing: only manual
  mode can express one, because upgrade mode rejects `--album` on its own and a batch line is trimmed
  before it is parsed, so a line written as `" - Album"` is read as an artist-only line. An artist-naming run with a configured library path explains a
  staging-only download once it has one.
- **Authoritative artist discography** — artist-only manual runs resolve conceptual albums from MusicBrainz
  release groups (cached locally for 30 days) and then run one sequential `Artist Album` Soulseek search per
  eligible album, oldest first. The same authoritative resolution powers `discover` mode for every artist
  it sweeps — those that own a folder named after them. Release categories and optional MusicBrainz artist IDs are configurable; the
  previous folder heuristic remains the explicit opt-out and the visible fallback.
- **Quality filtering** — filter Soulseek results by file extension, minimum
  bitrate, excluded keywords, and upload availability. With
  `download.max_queue_length: 0` a peer must offer a free upload slot; a
  positive limit also admits zero-slot peers until their reported queue
  position can be validated. Path-traversal names are rejected.
- **Peer reputation** — remembers each peer's effective throughput (bytes ÷ transfer time: retry delays plus
  the final transfer, excluding queue wait) and success rate (in SQLite), and ranks search results by a blend
  of advertised and measured throughput plus a reliability factor, so fast, reliable peers are preferred and
  slow or error-prone peers are demoted — regardless of what you search for. Controlled by

Modes: **upgrade** (ex-auto), **discover** (MusicBrainz gap-filling), **manual**, **batch**. Branch `main`, HEAD `171f65c` = tag **v0.30.0** = `origin/main`, working tree **clean**.

- **The question in play is ordering, not correctness of the MB lookup.** README documents discover as: *derive the artist list from your library (tags first, folder names as fallback) → keep only artists that own a folder → **ask MusicBrainz** which conceptual albums each is missing → download only those*. So the library scan is an unavoidable precursor to the MusicBrainz artist-existence check, which is exactly what the user wants inverted for an explicitly named artist.

- **The failure mode the user describes is an existing, user-visible error path:** `artist <x> was not found in the library; discover mode can only narrow to artists already present` — a *configuration error* raised from the library-derived index, i.e. before any MusicBrainz call. Nothing currently verifies the name against MusicBrainz first, so an unknown artist costs the whole scan and then dies with a message about the *library*, not about MusicBrainz.

- **Concrete cost observed in the reported run:** `Library scan complete: 2114 audio file(s), 196 album(s), 0 unreadable file(s) in 1.4s` — small at this library size, but the scan scales with library size while the MusicBrainz answer does not, and the scan also gates the artist validation that was wanted first.

- **Most recent shipped work (v0.30.0, `3395e9e`, 2026-10-05) touched exactly this seam:** `--artist`-named artists that the album-derived index does not hold are now resolved against the library's *folders*; `select_artists` gained a folder-evidence argument that the runner resolves **lazily and only for a name the index lacks** (automatic sweep unchanged, no extra directory walk); `SelectedArtist`'s two loose fields became one `ArtistDestination` (`Folder { library_root, artist_dir }` | `Staging`). Any reordering work will edit the same `src/runner.rs` ↔ `src/discover.rs` boundary and must preserve the sweep behaviour.

- **MusicBrainz machinery already exists and is reusable for a pre-scan check:** authoritative discography resolution from MusicBrainz release groups, **cached locally for 30 days** (per prior `discography-failure-cache` work), release categories via `discography.allowed_types`, and an optional `discography.artist_mbids` name→UUID map for ambiguous names. A fail-fast artist check would plausibly sit in front of the scan and share this cache rather than introduce a new client.

- **Prior art and specs that this change would supersede or extend:** `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-musicbrainz-library-gap-filling-design.md` (the artist-list-from-library contract), `2026-09-15-discover-library-placement-design.md` (folder/destination rules), `2026-09-13-dominant-musicbrainz-artist-resolution-design.md` (artist resolution). The newest spec/plan pair is `2026-09-29-rename-auto-mode-to-upgrade`; the 2026-10-05 fix updated existing specs with dated `Superseded on …` notes rather than adding a new pair — an established convention worth matching.

## Design — nested staging album layout (`src/staging.rs`)

### 1. Architecture and components

A new module `src/staging.rs` owns the staging layout rule; `organizer.rs` keeps library-write concerns. Four public items:

```rust
/// <staging_dir>/<sanitised artist>            (sanitize_component yields "_" for a blank artist)
pub fn artist_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str) -> PathBuf;
/// <staging_dir>/<sanitised artist>/<sanitised album>
pub fn album_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str, album: &str) -> PathBuf;

/// One album found under the staging root, with its identity resolved from the
/// processed-album table (None when no row matches: an untracked leftover).
pub struct StagedAlbum {
    pub album_dir: PathBuf,
    pub artist_dir_path: PathBuf,
    pub dir_album: String,
    pub identity: Option<StagedIdentity>, // { artist, album, status } - raw names from the DB
}
pub fn scan(staging_dir: &Path, db: &Database) -> Result<Vec<StagedAlbum>>;

/// Rename legacy `<artist>--<album>` folders into the nested form and drop
/// artist folders that hold nothing.
pub fn normalise_layout(staging_dir: &Path) -> Result<MigrationReport>;
```

`runner.rs:512` becomes `staging::album_dir(staging_dir, artist, album)`; every other staging path in `runner.rs` (`finish_library_write`, `discard_refused_staging`) derives from that one value, so the layout rule exists in one place. `organizer::parse_album_slug` **stays**, but only as the legacy parser `normalise_layout` uses — it is no longer used by recovery. `disc_subdir` takes the album string it can already see and stops walking when the directory name equals `sanitize_component(album)` instead of sniffing `"--"`.

*Does section 1 look right?*

### 2. Data flow

1. `process_albums` creates the staging root, then calls `staging::normalise_layout` (unconditional — the layout rule applies to every mode), then `organizer::recover_interrupted_upgrades` (unchanged gate: `library_upgrade.enabled` and a configured library path).
2. `process_album_internal` builds `album_staging = staging::album_dir(...)`; `download_album` creates it lazily and nests disc folders inside it exactly as today — no change to `download.rs`, because it receives the finished path.
3. On a library write, `finish_library_write` removes the album dir and then prunes its parent with `fs::remove_dir`; `discard_refused_staging` does the same once `remove_empty_staging_dirs` has emptied it. `remove_dir` refuses a non-empty directory, so a sibling album of the same artist staged concurrently is never touched.
4. Recovery iterates `staging::scan(...)` output and keeps its current two arms — `success` → `resume_library_upgrade(config, album_dir, library_root, raw artist, raw album)`, anything else → `remove_dir_all`. `resume_library_upgrade` and its library-write half are unchanged.

*Does section 2 look right?*

### 3. Legacy migration

`normalise_layout` walks the top level of the staging root:

- A directory whose name contains `--` is a legacy slug: split on the **first** `--` (today's rule), sanitise both halves, `create_dir_all` the artist dir, then `fs::rename` the legacy dir onto `<artist>/<album>`.
- If `<artist>/<album>` already exists, merge without overwriting: rename each child that is not already present at the destination and count it; when a name collides, the destination file stays and the legacy copy is left where it is. A legacy dir that still holds skipped entries is left in place and reported; one that is emptied is removed.
- A top-level name with no `--` is already an artist dir: it is left alone, and removed only if it holds nothing at all.
- A name that is not valid UTF-8 is left untouched with a warning: renaming it through `to_string_lossy` would invent characters and could orphan a recoverable album.

Per-entry failures are logged and counted, never fatal — the caller already treats a failed staging pass as a warning (`runner.rs:1469`), and a wasted rename must not stop a download run.

*Does section 3 look right?*

### 4. Recovery identity, and the edges

`scan` reads `db.get_processed_albums()` **once** per run and matches each `<artist>/<album>` directory against rows by comparing `sanitize_component(row.artist)` / `sanitize_component(row.album)` case-insensitively with the two directory names. A match yields the row's **raw** names and status, so `resume_library_upgrade` copies to the same library path (sanitising is idempotent) and the status write keeps the raw key. When several rows match, the highest `id` wins and the ambiguity is warned about, so a shared sanitised name still recovers the most recent successful one. No row → `identity: None` → the leftover is cleaned exactly as today.

Edge cases, each with a stated outcome: a blank artist (album-only run) stages under the `_` placeholder — uniform two-level layout, and no DB row means recovery cleans it exactly as it cleans `--Album` today; a legacy dir with no separator that holds no subdirectory is left alone and reported rather than deleted, because the nested layout makes "files directly in a top-level dir" ambiguous with real content; an album literally named `Disc 1` is unaffected because `disc_subdir` still returns the *innermost* match and the album root comparison only stops the upward walk. Staging inside a library path stays a documented misconfiguration, not a new validation — out of scope here.

*Does section 4 look right?*

### 5. Testing and documentation

Unit tests in `staging.rs`: both components sanitised; blank artist → `_`; migration of `A--B` to `A/B`; merge keeps the existing destination file and moves the rest; a still-populated legacy dir is reported not deleted; empty artist dirs pruned; a non-UTF-8 name skipped (`#[cfg(unix)]`); `scan` resolving raw names case-insensitively, returning `None` for an unknown dir, and choosing the highest `id` when two rows match. TDD: the failing test for each unit lands before its production code.

Documentation: a new dated spec at `docs/agent/specs/<date>-nested-staging-layout-design.md` plus its plan in `docs/agent/plans/`. # Nested staging album layout

## Problem

A staged album is one directory named `<artist>--<album>` directly under
`storage.staging_dir`, so a download that stays in staging reads as
`downloads/staging/Artist Name--Album Name/01 - Track.flac`. The operator wants the
two components to be real directories instead:
`downloads/staging/Artist Name/Album Name/01 - Track.flac`.

The flattened name is not only cosmetic. It is a lossy encoding of two values into one
path component, and the code that consumes it has to decode it again:

| Site | Behaviour today |
| --- | --- |
| `src/runner.rs:508-516` | Builds `format!("{}--{}", artist.replace(['/','\\'], "-"), album.unwrap_or("unknown").replace(['/','\\'], "-"))` and joins it to the staging root. |
| `src/organizer.rs:516-533` `disc_subdir` | Walks a staged file's parent directories and stops when a directory name `.contains("--")`, because that names the album staging root. An album whose own name contains `--` cannot be told from a boundary by this test. |
| `src/organizer.rs:758-763` `parse_album_slug` | Splits on the first `--` to recover `(artist, album)`; a name without a separator becomes album `"Unknown"`. |
| `src/organizer.rs:774-810` `recover_interrupted_upgrades` | Reads the top level of the staging root, treats every directory as an album slug, re-verifies a `success` album by copying it back, and deletes every other leftover. |
| `src/runner.rs:355-389` `discard_refused_staging` | Removes a refused album's staged files, then prunes directories that are now empty. Its warnings explain the `A--B` + `C` versus `A` + `B--C` slug collapse. |
| `src/runner.rs:392-413` `finish_library_write` | Removes the album staging directory after the album has been written to the library. |

## Goal

A completed download stages under `<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/`, for every mode, with
both components produced by the same sanitiser the library write uses, and with no
behaviour change anywhere else: same recovery semantics, same cleanup, same database keys.

## Scope

### In scope

- The staging path layout and every site that builds or decodes it.
- A startup migration for staging directories left by earlier versions.
- The recovery scan's album-identity lookup, which the new layout and the sanitiser change.
- Cleanup of the artist level when an album leaves staging.
- An audit that records, and tests that enforce, one sanitiser for every folder seakarr
  creates.

### Out of scope

- The library layout, which is already `<library root>/<artist>/<album>/` and does not change.
- Placement semantics: placement still never creates an artist folder, and still writes only

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

# Nested staging album layout

## Problem

A staged album is one directory named `<artist>--<album>` directly under
`storage.staging_dir`, so a download that stays in staging reads as
`downloads/staging/Artist Name--Album Name/01 - Track.flac`. The operator wants the
two components to be real directories instead:
`downloads/staging/Artist Name/Album Name/01 - Track.flac`.

The flattened name is not only cosmetic. It is a lossy encoding of two values into one
path component, and the code that consumes it has to decode it again:

| Site | Behaviour today |
| --- | --- |
| `src/runner.rs:508-516` | Builds `format!("{}--{}", artist.replace(['/','\\'], "-"), album.unwrap_or("unknown").replace(['/','\\'], "-"))` and joins it to the staging root. |
| `src/organizer.rs:516-533` `disc_subdir` | Walks a staged file's parent directories and stops when a directory name `.contains("--")`, because that names the album staging root. An album whose own name contains `--` cannot be told from a boundary by this test. |
| `src/organizer.rs:758-763` `parse_album_slug` | Splits on the first `--` to recover `(artist, album)`; a name without a separator becomes album `"Unknown"`. |
| `src/organizer.rs:774-810` `recover_interrupted_upgrades` | Reads the top level of the staging root, treats every directory as an album slug, re-verifies a `success` album by copying it back, and deletes every other leftover. |
| `src/runner.rs:355-389` `discard_refused_staging` | Removes a refused album's staged files, then prunes directories that are now empty. Its warnings explain the `A--B` + `C` versus `A` + `B--C` slug collapse. |
| `src/runner.rs:392-413` `finish_library_write` | Removes the album staging directory after the album has been written to the library. |

## Goal

A completed download stages under `<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/`, for every mode, with
both components produced by the same sanitiser the library write uses, and with no
behaviour change anywhere else: same recovery semantics, same cleanup, same database keys.

## Scope

### In scope

- The staging path layout and every site that builds or decodes it.
- A startup migration for staging directories left by earlier versions.
- The recovery scan's album-identity lookup, which the new layout and the sanitiser change.
- Cleanup of the artist level when an album leaves staging.
- An audit that records, and tests that enforce, one sanitiser for every folder seakarr
  creates.

### Out of scope

- The library layout, which is already `<library root>/<artist>/<album>/` and does not change.
- Placement semantics: placement still never creates an artist folder, and still writes only
  into an artist folder the library already holds.
- Any new or changed configuration key. `storage.staging_dir` keeps its meaning and default
  (`downloads/staging`).
- A validation that `storage.staging_dir` sits outside every `library.paths` entry. The
  README documents the requirement; this change does not add a gate.
- Disc subdirectory nesting inside an album (`download.rs`), which is unchanged because it
  receives the finished album path.
- Historical design documents that record the old layout
  (`docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-discover-library-placement-design.md:14`,
  `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-23-remove-organize-design.md:209`). They are dated records and
  are left as written.

## Decisions

### Staging albums are two path components

`<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/`. The artist level exists for every album, including an
album-only manual run, which names no artist. That keeps one rule, and therefore one
recovery walk, instead of a layout whose depth depends on which request produced it.

### Both components use `sanitize_component`

The artist component and the album component each pass through
`organizer::sanitize_component`, the function every library write already uses: Windows
reserved characters and control characters are removed, a trailing dot or space is trimmed,
a reserved device name is prefixed (`CON` becomes `_CON`), and a value that sanitises to
nothing becomes `_`.

Consequences, all deliberate:

- The staging tree mirrors the library tree for the same album, so a folder name that
  renders correctly in the library renders correctly in staging too.
- An album-only run (blank artist) stages under the `_` placeholder:
  `<staging_dir>/_/<album>/`. `_` is the sanitiser's existing placeholder for "this value
  keeps nothing", and `ArtistFolderIndex` already refuses to treat `_` as an artist folder
  (`src/discover.rs:319-320`), so the placeholder cannot be mistaken for a library match.
- An artist-only run that names no album keeps today's `"unknown"` album component:
  `<staging_dir>/<artist>/unknown/`.

### A new `src/staging.rs` owns the layout

The layout rule, the migration, and the staging scan move into one small module. This
follows the crate's existing idiom (`discs.rs`, `tracks.rs`, `report.rs`) and keeps the two
riskiest behaviours of this change — a merge that must never overwrite, and a name lookup
that must resolve a sanitised directory back to a raw album — unit-testable without a
runner, a client, or a download.

`organizer.rs` keeps the library half of recovery (`resume_library_upgrade`) and the
sanitiser. `runner.rs` keeps orchestration and calls into the module.

### Legacy `<artist>--<album>` folders are migrated at startup

`normalise_layout` runs once per run, before the recovery scan, and is **not** gated on
`library_upgrade.enabled`: the layout rule belongs to staging, not to one mode. It renames
each top-level `<artist>--<album>` directory into the nested form, so a leftover from an
earlier version is still found by the recovery scan and by the operator.

`parse_album_slug` is kept, renamed in documentation as the legacy parser, and used only by
the migration. It is removed from the recovery path.

### Migration merges without overwriting

Migrating a legacy directory whose nested destination already exists must not destroy
either copy:

- Rename each entry that is absent at the destination, recursing into subdirectories so a
  legacy `CD 01/` folder keeps its shape.
- When a name already exists at the destination, keep the destination file and leave the
  legacy copy where it is. Nothing is overwritten.
- A legacy directory that the merge emptied is removed. A legacy directory that still holds
  a skipped entry is left in place and reported, naming the first entry that stopped it —
  the same shape of warning `discard_refused_staging` already emits.

### Recovery resolves identity by a sanitised match

`recover_interrupted_upgrades` identifies an album by looking a directory name up in the
`processed_albums` table, which stores raw names (`db.get_album_status`). With sanitised
directory names, an exact lookup would miss (`Gold: Greatest Hits` stages as
`Gold_ Greatest Hits`), and a missed lookup means the leftover is deleted as untracked
debris — data loss for an interrupted upgrade that was about to be recovered.

`staging::scan` therefore loads `db.get_processed_albums()` once and matches each
`<artist>/<album>` directory against rows by comparing `sanitize_component(row.artist)` and
`sanitize_component(row.album)` with the two directory names, case-insensitively. A match
yields the row's **raw** names and status, which are what `resume_library_upgrade` needs:
it sanitises them again for the library destination (sanitising is idempotent, so the
destination is unchanged) and the status write keeps the raw key. No row yields no
identity, and the leftover is cleaned exactly as today.

When several rows match, the highest `id` wins and the ambiguity is warned about, so the
most recently tried album is the one recovered.

### `disc_subdir` stops at the album root by name, not by a separator

`disc_subdir` currently stops walking when a parent directory name contains `--`. It is
called from exactly one place, `organizer.rs:426` inside `copy_into_library`, where the
album string is already in scope, so it instead stops when the directory name equals
`sanitize_component(album)` — the album staging directory's own name. This is the same
boundary without the separator sniff, and the innermost-match-first walk still returns a
real disc folder before it reaches the album root, so a multi-disc album whose own name
carries an embedded disc marker (`Gold (Disc 1)`) behaves as it does today.

### An empty artist directory is pruned

The artist level is a directory seakarr creates, so it is removed when it holds nothing:

- Immediately, by `finish_library_write` and `discard_refused_staging`, once the album
  directory they handle has gone.
- Elsewhere, by `normalise_layout` at the start of the next run, which removes an artist
  directory that holds no entries at all. This covers a failure path that removed an album
  directory and left its parent behind.

`fs::remove_dir` refuses a non-empty directory, so an artist's second album, staged
concurrently or left from an interrupted run, can never be removed by this.

### Sanitisation is consistent across every library write

One rule, one function: every production path that turns an artist or album string into a
path component calls `sanitize_component` at the moment the name is created. There is no
second sanitiser and no per-mode variant. Staging joins that set.

The audit below records the state this change must preserve, so a later reader can tell a
deliberate exception from an oversight:

| Library-write path | Artist component | Album and file components |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy_to_library` (`organizer.rs:328` → `library_relative_path:129-134`) | `sanitize_component(artist)` | `sanitize_component(album/track/title/ext)` |
| `place_into_library` (`album_dir_for:145-158`) | the existing on-disk folder name, used **verbatim** | `sanitize_component(album)` |
| `delete_lesser_quality_files:545-554` | sanitised | sanitised |
| `resume_library_upgrade:696-698`, per-entry leaf `:723`/`:728` | sanitised | sanitised |
| `disc_subdir:531` (a disc label becomes a real folder) | n/a | sanitised |
| `search.rs:1211-1256`, `discover.rs:319-320` (lookups, both sides) | sanitised | sanitised |
| staged file names (`download.rs`) | n/a | peer basename, `safe_basename`-checked; never a library folder |

The single exception is `place_into_library`, and it is deliberate: its `artist_dir` is the
name of an artist folder that already exists on disk, found by the library walk or
`ArtistFolderIndex`, and placement exists to write *into* that folder rather than create a
differently-named one beside it. Re-sanitising it would not add safety — `album_dir_for`
already rejects any value that is not a single ordinary path component — it would split one
artist across two folders. Every folder seakarr *creates* comes from a sanitised name.

## Architecture

### `src/staging.rs` (new)

```rust
/// `<staging_dir>/<sanitized artist>`.
pub fn artist_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str) -> PathBuf;

/// `<staging_dir>/<sanitized artist>/<sanitized album>`.
/// `None` keeps today's `"unknown"` album component.
pub fn album_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str, album: Option<&str>) -> PathBuf;

/// One album found under the staging root.
pub struct StagedAlbum {
    /// `<staging_dir>/<artist>` — the level to prune when the album leaves.
    pub artist_dir_path: PathBuf,
    /// `<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>`.
    pub album_dir_path: PathBuf,
    /// The album directory name as it is on disk (the sanitised component).
    pub dir_album: String,
    /// `None` when no `processed_albums` row matches: an untracked leftover.
    pub identity: Option<StagedIdentity>,
}

/// Raw names and status, as stored in the database.
pub struct StagedIdentity {
    pub artist: String,
    pub album: String,
    pub status: String,
}

/// Walk the two levels under the staging root and resolve each album's identity.
pub fn scan(staging_dir: &Path, db: &Database) -> Result<Vec<StagedAlbum>>;

/// Rename legacy `<artist>--<album>` directories into the nested form, prune artist
/// directories that hold nothing, and report what happened. A missing staging root
/// is not an error: there is nothing stale in a directory that does not exist.
pub fn normalise_layout(staging_dir: &Path) -> Result<MigrationReport>;

/// The one call a run makes before it stages anything: create the staging root if
/// it is missing, then `normalise_layout`. Replaces the bare
/// `std::fs::create_dir_all(staging_dir)` each mode performs today.
pub fn prepare(staging_dir: &Path) -> Result<MigrationReport>;

pub struct MigrationReport {
    /// Legacy directories renamed wholesale: the nested destination was absent.
    pub migrated: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Legacy directories merged into a destination that already existed.
    pub merged: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// A legacy directory left in place, with the first entry that stopped it.
    pub left_in_place: Vec<(PathBuf, PathBuf)>,
    /// A top-level directory that is neither a legacy slug nor an artist directory.
    pub unrecognised: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Names that are not valid UTF-8; renaming them lossily could orphan an album.

[236 more lines in file. Use offset=241 to continue.]

/// Names that are not valid UTF-8; renaming them lossily could orphan an album.
    pub non_utf8: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub failed: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>,
    pub pruned_artist_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,
}
```

### `src/runner.rs`

- `process_album_internal` builds `album_staging = staging::album_dir(staging_dir, artist, album)`
  in place of the `format!("{}--{}", ...)` slug. Every other use of the album staging path in
  the file (`finish_library_write`, `discard_refused_staging`, the `DownloadDestination::Staging`
  value, log lines) derives from that one value.
- `finish_library_write` prunes the artist level after removing the album directory.
- `discard_refused_staging` prunes the artist level once `remove_empty_staging_dirs` reports
  the album directory gone, and its warnings describe the nested name instead of the
  `artist--album` collapse. The collapse cannot occur in the new layout, because the two
  values are separate path components.
- Each mode's existing `let staging_dir = Path::new(&config.storage.staging_dir);` /
  `std::fs::create_dir_all(staging_dir)?` pair becomes `staging::prepare(staging_dir)`:
  `run_upgrade_mode` (`runner.rs:1465`), `run_manual_mode` (`runner.rs:2975`), and
  `run_batch_mode` (`main.rs:737`). `run_discover_mode` (`runner.rs:2465`) has no staging
  setup today — it passes the configured path straight to `process_album` — so it gains one
  `staging::prepare` call, which also creates a staging root that `download_album` currently
  creates lazily.
- `run_upgrade_mode` then calls `organizer::recover_interrupted_upgrades`, unchanged in
  gate, position, and effect. Recovery stays where it is: manual, discover, and batch runs
  do not scan staging for interrupted upgrades today, and this change does not add that.
  Both staging calls keep the existing treatment: a failure is logged as a warning and never
  aborts the run.

### `src/organizer.rs`

- `sanitize_component` stays here; `staging.rs` calls it. It is not duplicated or moved.
- `parse_album_slug` stays as the legacy parser, used only by `staging::normalise_layout`,
  and leaves the recovery path.
- `disc_subdir` takes the album component and stops on a name match instead of `contains("--")`.
- `recover_interrupted_upgrades` keeps its signature, its gate (`library_upgrade.enabled`
  and a configured library path), and its two arms, but iterates `staging::scan(...)` instead
  of reading directory names: `Some(identity)` with status `success` resumes the copy with
  the identity's raw names, and everything else — a failed status, a non-success status, no
  identity at all — removes the album directory as debris.

### `src/download.rs`

Unchanged. It receives the album path, creates it on demand, and nests disc folders inside
it.

## Data flow

1. A run starts and calls `staging::prepare(staging_dir)`, from each mode's entry point:
   `run_upgrade_mode`, `run_discover_mode`, `run_manual_mode`, and `run_batch_mode` in
   `main.rs`. It creates the staging root if missing, then renames each legacy
   `<artist>--<album>` directory into `<artist>/<album>` (merging when the destination
   exists), removes empty artist directories, and logs and records every anomaly.
2. `organizer::recover_interrupted_upgrades` runs in upgrade mode under its existing gate:
   it scans the two levels, resolves each album's raw identity by the sanitised match, copies
   a `success` album into the library, and deletes anything else. The other modes stage no
   recovery scan, as today.
3. `process_album_internal` computes `<staging>/<sanitize(artist)>/<sanitize(album)>`.
   `download_album` creates the album directory only when a peer will really deliver files,
   and keeps its existing per-disc nesting inside it.
4. A library write copies the album into the library, then `finish_library_write` removes the
   album staging directory and prunes the artist directory if it is now empty. A download
   that stays in staging keeps both levels, and its reported destination names the nested path.
5. A refused album's staged files are removed, the album directory is pruned when empty, and
   the artist directory is pruned the same way.

## Error handling

| Situation | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Migration cannot rename or merge an entry | The entry is recorded in `failed` with its error, the run continues, and the startup call logs a warning. A wasted rename never aborts a download run. |
| A legacy directory still holds a skipped entry after the merge | Left in place, recorded in `left_in_place` with the first entry that stopped it, and warned about. No file is overwritten. |
| A top-level directory name is not valid UTF-8 | Left untouched and recorded in `non_utf8`. Renaming it through the lossy conversion would invent characters and could orphan a recoverable album. |
| A top-level directory with no `--` holds no subdirectory | Left in place and recorded in `unrecognised`. In a nested layout the meaning of files directly in a top-level directory is ambiguous, and deleting real content is worse than leaving junk. |
| A legacy directory was left in place | Re-examined on the next run: the migration is idempotent, so a directory the operator resolved migrates then, and one that is still blocked warns again rather than being deleted. |
| Several `processed_albums` rows match the sanitised names | The highest `id` wins; the ambiguity is warned about with both raw names. |
| No `processed_albums` row matches | `identity: None`, and the album directory is removed as untracked debris, exactly as an unmatched `artist--album` directory is today. |
| A blank artist (album-only run) | Stages under `_`; it writes no `processed_albums` row (`mark_album_processed_if_identifiable` returns early for a blank artist), so recovery cleans it as it cleans `--Album` today. |
| Pruning an artist directory that holds a sibling album | `fs::remove_dir` fails on a non-empty directory; the failure is ignored, and the sibling is untouched. |
| An unwritable staging root | Surfaces through the existing `?` on the staging setup, unchanged from today. |

## Backward compatibility

- **Configuration:** no key is added, removed, or reinterpreted. `storage.staging_dir`
  keeps its default and meaning.
- **Database:** `processed_albums` keeps raw `artist`/`album` values and case-insensitive
  lookups. Only the recovery lookup changes, from an exact key to a sanitised match, which
  makes it resolve names it previously missed rather than miss names it previously resolved.
- **Existing staging content:** migrated on the next run. The migration is one-way. An older
  binary run against a migrated staging directory would treat each artist directory as an
  album slug (`Artist` → album `Unknown`), find no matching row, and delete the album
  directories below it as untracked debris. Reverting to an older version therefore requires
  an empty staging directory; the release note must say so.
- **Log and report wording:** paths shown to the operator change shape, because the
  destination really changed. No wording that names a mode, an outcome, or a reason changes.

## Deliberate limits

- The legacy decode inherits the ambiguity the old format always had: a legacy directory
  name containing `--` splits at the first occurrence, so an artist whose own name contains
  `--` is attributed as today. The migration is the last place this ambiguity exists.
- Migration uses `parse_album_slug`'s first-occurrence split and nothing else: it does not
  attempt to reinterpret a legacy name written by a version whose slug rules differed.
- A staging directory that is not writable is not repaired; the run reports the failure and
  continues, as it does today.
- Pruning is deliberately non-recursive beyond the album directory: an artist directory is
  removed only when it is empty, never when it holds anything seakarr cannot attribute.

## Testing

### Staging module tests (`staging.rs`)

- `album_dir` sanitises both components; a hostile title (`Gold: Greatest Hits`, `???`,
  `CON`, `A/B`) and one ending in a trailing space yield the same components the library
  write would use.
- `album_dir` with a blank artist yields the `_` level; with `album: None` yields the
  `unknown` level.
- `prepare` creates a missing staging root and reports an empty migration; a second call
  over an already-nested tree reports nothing and changes nothing.
- `normalise_layout` renames `Artist--Album` to `Artist/Album`, recursion included, so a
  legacy `CD 01/track.flac` keeps its shape.
- `normalise_layout` merges into an existing nested album: the destination file wins, the
  other file moves, and a directory still holding a skipped entry is reported in
  `left_in_place` and not deleted.
- `normalise_layout` prunes an empty artist directory and leaves one that holds anything.
- `normalise_layout` leaves a byte-invalid name alone (`#[cfg(unix)]`).
- `scan` resolves a sanitised directory name back to the raw names in the database,
  case-insensitively; returns no identity for an unknown album directory; and picks the
  highest `id` when two rows match.
- A consistency test: for one hostile album title, the two staging components equal the two
  library destination components.

### Recovery tests (`organizer.rs`)

- The recovery tests move to nested fixtures (`<root>/Artist/Album`) in place of
  `Unknown--Album`, keeping their three cases: a `success` album is copied back, a `failed`
  album is cleaned, an untracked album is cleaned.
- `disc_subdir` still excludes the embedded-marker album root and still returns an inner
  disc folder, for both a dedicated (`CD 01`) and an embedded (`Gold (Disc 1)`) marker.
- `parse_album_slug` keeps its cases as the legacy parser.

### Runner cleanup tests (`runner.rs`)

- A library write leaves neither the album directory nor an empty artist directory behind.
- A refused download leaves no empty artist directory behind, and a sibling album staged
  under the same artist is never removed.
- An album-only run stages under `_/<album>` and still reports a staging destination.
- A discovery run migrates a legacy staging directory before it stages an album, proving
  the mode that had no staging setup now has one.
- A failure path that removes an album directory leaves the artist directory for the next
  run's `normalise_layout` to prune.

### End-to-end placement test (`tests/pipeline_test.rs`)

- The end-to-end staging fixture expects `<staging>/Test Artist/Test Album` and asserts the
  nested tree is gone after a successful placement.

### Download tests (`download.rs`)

- Unchanged tests must pass. One added assertion: a multi-disc album produces
  `Artist/Album/CD 01/...` inside the album directory, proving the disc nesting is still
  relative to the album root.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A completed download for artist `A` and album `B` stages at `<staging_dir>/<san(A)>/<san(B)>/`,
   in every mode: `upgrade`, `discover`, manual, and batch.
2. Every folder name seakarr creates, in staging and in the library, comes from
   `sanitize_component`; the only name used unsanitised is the existing on-disk artist folder
   in `place_into_library`, with its guard unchanged.
3. A legacy `<artist>--<album>` directory is renamed into the nested layout on the next run,
   and a nested destination that already exists is merged without overwriting a single file.
4. An interrupted library upgrade is still recovered after the change, including for an album
   title whose sanitised directory name differs from the stored raw name.
5. The `processed_albums` keys, the SQLite schema, the configuration schema, and the search,
   ranking, and placement behaviours are unchanged.
6. No empty artist directory is left in staging after a completed, refused, or failed album,
   and no sibling album directory is ever removed by cleanup.
7. Every mode that can stage a download performs the migration: `upgrade`, `discover`,
   manual, and batch.
8. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` pass.

## Documentation

- This spec, and its plan in `docs/agent/plans/`, follow the repository convention for
  non-trivial work.
- The README describes `storage.staging_dir` without naming the layout, so it needs no
  change; the implementer confirms that no table or paragraph in it names
  `<artist>--<album>` before concluding that.
- A dated design decision recording the superseded layout already exists
  (`docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-discover-library-placement-design.md`,
  `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-23-remove-organize-design.md`); those files are left as written.
- The one-way migration is called out in the release note for the version that ships it.

## Alternatives considered

**Keep the flat name, change the separator.** Replacing `--` with a character an artist name
cannot contain would fix the boundary test but not the request, and no character is both
safe on every filesystem and excluded from every metadata value.

**Sanitise the album component only.** Leaves the artist level as the one staging folder
whose name is not portable, which is the defect the library sanitiser exists to prevent, and
puts staging and library artist folders out of step.

**Keep the layout rule in `organizer.rs`.** Smallest diff, but the layout rule would stay
split between `runner.rs` (build) and `organizer.rs` (decode, recovery), which is what made
this change touch so many sites.

**Thread a typed `StagingAlbum` value through every call.** Stronger typing, but it changes
`download.rs` signatures and many call sites in a 10,700-line `runner.rs` for a layout change,
and the same guarantee is available from a single constructor plus a path comparison.

**A sidecar manifest recording the raw artist and album.** Lossless even when two raw names
sanitise to one directory name, but it puts a non-audio file inside every staged album, which
the placement and resume walks would then have to exclude from the library copy.

**Sanitise the existing artist folder name in `place_into_library`.** Rejected: the folder
already exists under that name, so sanitising it would write the album into a second artist
folder beside the real one.

- `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-discover-library-placement-design.md` — placement never
  creates an artist folder.

# Nested staging album layout Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use sub-agents (recommended) to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Stage every download under `<storage.staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>/` instead of `<storage.staging_dir>/<artist>--<album>/`, migrating existing legacy directories on startup.

**Architecture:** A new `src/staging.rs` owns the layout rule (`artist_dir`, `album_dir`), the startup migration (`normalise_layout`, `prepare`) and the staging scan (`scan`, which resolves a sanitised directory name back to the raw `processed_albums` row). `organizer.rs` keeps the sanitiser and the library half of recovery; `runner.rs` and `main.rs` call `staging::prepare` from each mode entry point and derive every album staging path from `staging::album_dir`.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024, `rusqlite` (SQLite), `tokio`, `tracing`, `tempfile` for tests. No new dependency.

**Spec:** `docs/agent/specs/2026-10-08-nested-staging-album-layout-design.md` (approved, commit `542309e`).

> **Plan location note:** the invoking chain asked for `docs/plans/`. The repository convention (`AGENTS.md` rule 7, and every plan since `docs/agent/plans/2026-09-09-queue-aware-download-timeouts.md`) is `docs/agent/plans/`. This plan follows the repository convention; `docs/plans/` is a legacy directory holding pre-convention plans only.

---

## Scope Check

Single subsystem. The spec changes the staging path layout in one crate, with one new module. It is not separable into independent plans: the construction site, the decode sites, the migration and the recovery lookup must land together or staging holds two layouts at once and recovery deletes real albums as debris. **No split.**

## File Structure

| File | Responsibility after this change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/staging.rs` (new) | The staging layout rule, the legacy migration, and the staging scan with identity resolution. |
| `src/lib.rs` (modify) | Declare `pub mod staging;`. |
| `src/organizer.rs` (modify) | Keeps `sanitize_component`, `parse_album_slug` (legacy parser), `resume_library_upgrade`. `disc_subdir` gains an album-component parameter; `recover_interrupted_upgrades` iterates `staging::scan`. |
| `src/runner.rs` (modify) | `process_album_internal` builds the nested album path; `finish_library_write` and `discard_refused_staging` prune the artist level; three mode entry points call `staging::prepare`. |
| `src/main.rs` (modify) | `run_batch_mode` calls `staging::prepare`. |
| `src/download.rs` (modify) | One added test assertion only. Production code unchanged. |
| `tests/pipeline_test.rs` (modify) | The end-to-end staging fixture expects the nested tree. |

Order matters: Tasks 1-5 build `staging.rs` with no production caller, so the suite stays green. Task 6 changes `disc_subdir` (its one caller is updated in the same task). Task 7 switches recovery over. Task 8 switches the runner and sweeps the runner test fixtures. Task 9 wires the mode entry points. Task 10 finishes the end-to-end and documentation work.

---

### Task 1: `staging.rs` foundation — `artist_dir` and `album_dir`

```rust
//! The staging album layout.
//!
//! A staged album is two real directories — `<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>` —
//! rather than one flattened `<artist>--<album>` name. Both components are
//! produced by [`crate::organizer::sanitize_component`], the same sanitiser
//! every library write uses, so the staging tree mirrors the library tree for
//! the same album.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// The album component used when a run names no album. Matches the value the
/// flattened layout used, so an artist-only run's staging directory keeps the
/// name an operator already recognises.
pub const UNKNOWN_ALBUM: &str = "unknown";

/// `<staging_dir>/<sanitized artist>`.
pub fn artist_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str) -> PathBuf {
    todo!("sanitize the artist component")
}

/// `<staging_dir>/<sanitized artist>/<sanitized album>`.
///
/// `album: None` keeps the [`UNKNOWN_ALBUM`] component an artist-only run used
/// under the flattened layout.
pub fn album_dir(staging_dir: &Path, artist: &str, album: Option<&str>) -> PathBuf {
    todo!("sanitize both components")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::organizer::sanitize_component;

    #[test]
    fn artist_dir_sanitises_the_artist_component() {
        assert_eq!(
            artist_dir(Path::new("/staging"), "AC/DC"),
            Path::new("/staging/AC-DC"),
            "a path separator in an artist name must not create a level"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn album_dir_sanitises_the_album_component() {
        assert_eq!(
            album_dir(Path::new("/staging"), "Artist", Some("Gold: Greatest Hits")),
            Path::new("/staging/Artist/Gold Greatest Hits"),
            "a Windows-reserved character is removed by the library sanitiser"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn album_dir_uses_the_placeholder_for_a_component_that_sanitises_away() {
        assert_eq!(
            album_dir(Path::new("/staging"), "???", Some("Album")),
            Path::new("/staging/_/Album"),
            "a component that keeps nothing becomes the sanitiser's placeholder"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn album_dir_neutralises_a_reserved_device_name() {
        assert_eq!(
            album_dir(Path::new("/staging"), "Artist", Some("CON")),
            Path::new("/staging/Artist/_CON"),
            "a reserved device name is prefixed by the library sanitiser"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn album_dir_keeps_the_unknown_component_when_no_album_is_named() {
        assert_eq!(
            album_dir(Path::new("/staging"), "Artist", None),
            Path::new("/staging/Artist/unknown"),
            "an artist-only run keeps the album component it always had"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn album_dir_makes_an_album_only_run_a_two_level_tree() {
        assert_eq!(
            album_dir(Path::new("/staging"), "", Some("Orphan Album")),
            Path::new("/staging/_/Orphan Album"),
            "a blank artist still gets an artist level, so the tree depth is constant"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn album_dir_matches_the_library_components_for_a_hostile_title() {
        let staging = Path::new("/staging");
        let artist = "Gold: Greatest Hits";
        let album = "A/B .. ???";
        assert_eq!(
            album_dir(staging, artist, Some(album)),
            staging
                .join(sanitize_component(artist))
                .join(sanitize_component(album)),
            "staging must use one sanitiser, the same one the library write uses"
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
    fn normalise_layout_renames_a_legacy_slug_into_two_levels() {
```

```rust
/// What a [`normalise_layout`] pass changed, and what it could not.
///
/// Every field is a record for a warning, not an error: a wasted rename must
/// never abort a download run.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct MigrationReport {
    /// Legacy directories renamed wholesale: the nested destination was absent.
    pub migrated: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Legacy directories merged into a destination that already existed.
    pub merged: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// A legacy directory left in place, with the first entry that stopped it.
    pub left_in_place: Vec<(PathBuf, PathBuf)>,
    /// A top-level directory that is neither a legacy slug nor an artist directory.
    pub unrecognised: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Names that are not valid UTF-8; renaming them lossily could orphan an album.
    pub non_utf8: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// A directory whose rewrite failed, with the error.
    pub failed: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>,
    /// Empty artist directories removed.
    pub pruned_artist_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,
}

impl MigrationReport {
    /// Log every anomaly at the level an operator sees at startup.
    fn log_anomalies(&self) {
        for (path, error) in &self.failed {
            tracing::warn!("Staging migration could not rewrite {path:?}: {error}");
        }
        for path in &self.non_utf8 {
            tracing::warn!(
                "Staging migration left {path:?} untouched: its name is not valid UTF-8, and renaming it lossily could orphan an album"
            );
        }
        for (path, first) in &self.left_in_place {
            tracing::warn!(
                "Staging migration left {path:?} in place: {first:?} already exists at the destination and was not overwritten"
            );
        }
        for path in &self.unrecognised {
            tracing::warn!(
                "Staging holds {path:?}, which is neither a legacy artist--album directory nor an artist directory; leaving it untouched"
            );
        }
    }
}

/// Create the staging root if it is missing, then bring its layout up to date.
///
/// The one call a run makes before it stages anything. An anomaly is logged,
/// never returned as an error: the run's own failure surface is unchanged.
pub fn prepare(staging_dir: &Path) -> Result<MigrationReport> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(staging_dir)?;
    let report = normalise_layout(staging_dir)?;
    report.log_anomalies();
    Ok(report)
}

/// Rename legacy `<artist>--<album>` directories into `<artist>/<album>` and
/// remove artist directories that hold nothing. A missing staging root is not
/// an error: there is nothing stale in a directory that does not exist.
pub fn normalise_layout(staging_dir: &Path) -> Result<MigrationReport> {
    let mut report = MigrationReport::default();
    let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(staging_dir) {
        Ok(entries) => entries,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(report),
        Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
    };

    for entry in entries {
        let entry = match entry {
            Ok(entry) => entry,
            Err(e) => {
                report
                    .failed
                    .push((staging_dir.to_path_buf(), e.to_string()));
                continue;
            }
        };
        if !entry.file_type().map(|kind| kind.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false) {
            continue;
        }
        let path = entry.path();
        let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).map(str::to_owned) else {
            report.non_utf8.push(path);
            continue;
        };

        if !name.contains("--") {
            prune_or_report_artist_dir(&path, &mut report);
            continue;
        }

        let (artist, album) = crate::organizer::parse_album_slug(&name);
        let destination = artist_dir(staging_dir, &artist).join(
            crate::organizer::sanitize_component(&album),
        );
        if !destination.exists() {
            let parent = destination.parent().unwrap_or(staging_dir);
            match std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).and_then(|()| std::fs::rename(&path, &destination))
            {
                Ok(()) => report.migrated.push(path),
                Err(e) => report.failed.push((path, e.to_string())),
            }
        } else {
            report.left_in_place.push((path, destination));
        }
    }

    Ok(report)
}

/// Remove a top-level directory that holds nothing; report one that holds files
/// but no subdirectory, because in a nested layout that shape is ambiguous and
/// deleting real content is worse than leaving junk.
fn prune_or_report_artist_dir(path: &Path, report: &mut MigrationReport) {
    let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(path) else {
        report.failed.push((path.to_path_buf(), "unreadable".to_string()));
        return;
    };
    let mut holds_anything = false;
    let mut holds_a_subdirectory = false;
    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        holds_anything = true;
        if entry.file_type().map(|kind| kind.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false) {
            holds_a_subdirectory = true;
        }
    }
    if !holds_anything {
        match std::fs::remove_dir(path) {
            Ok(()) => report.pruned_artist_dirs.push(path.to_path_buf()),
            Err(e) => report.failed.push((path.to_path_buf(), e.to_string())),
        }
    } else if !holds_a_subdirectory {
        report.unrecognised.push(path.to_path_buf());
    }
}
```

```rust
/// What a merge left behind.
enum MergeOutcome {
    /// Every entry moved; the legacy directory is now empty.
    Emptied,
    /// A name already existed at the destination. Nothing was overwritten, and
    /// the first colliding source entry is named for the warning.
    Skipped(PathBuf),
}

/// Move every entry of `legacy` that is absent at `destination`, recursing so a
/// nested disc folder keeps its shape. A name that already exists at the
/// destination is never overwritten: the destination entry stays and the legacy
/// copy is left where it is.
fn merge_without_overwrite(legacy: &Path, destination: &Path) -> std::io::Result<MergeOutcome> {
    let mut first_skipped: Option<PathBuf> = None;
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(legacy)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let source = entry.path();
        let target = destination.join(entry.file_name());
        if target.exists() {
            first_skipped.get_or_insert(source);
            continue;
        }
        if entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&target)?;
            if let MergeOutcome::Skipped(first) = merge_without_overwrite(&source, &target)? {
                first_skipped.get_or_insert(first);
            } else {
                let _ = std::fs::remove_dir(&source);
            }
        } else {
            std::fs::rename(&source, &target)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(match first_skipped {
        Some(first) => MergeOutcome::Skipped(first),
        None => MergeOutcome::Emptied,
    })
}
```

```rust
/// One album found under the staging root.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct StagedAlbum {
    /// `<staging_dir>/<artist>` — the level to prune when the album leaves.
    pub artist_dir_path: PathBuf,
    /// `<staging_dir>/<artist>/<album>`.
    pub album_dir_path: PathBuf,
    /// The album directory name as it is on disk (the sanitised component).
    pub dir_album: String,
    /// `None` when no `processed_albums` row matches: an untracked leftover.
    pub identity: Option<StagedIdentity>,
}

/// Raw names and status, as stored in the database.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct StagedIdentity {
    pub artist: String,
    pub album: String,
    pub status: String,
}

/// Walk the two levels under the staging root and resolve each album's identity.
///
/// The directory names are sanitised while the database rows are raw, so an
/// exact lookup would miss a title such as `Gold: Greatest Hits` and the
/// leftover would be deleted as debris. Rows are matched by sanitising both
/// sides, case-insensitively, which is what the database's own `COLLATE NOCASE`
/// lookup does.
pub fn scan(staging_dir: &Path, db: &crate::db::Database) -> Result<Vec<StagedAlbum>> {
    let rows = db.get_processed_albums()?;
    let mut albums = Vec::new();
    let artist_entries = match std::fs::read_dir(staging_dir) {
        Ok(entries) => entries,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(albums),
        Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
    };

    for artist_entry in artist_entries {
        let artist_entry = artist_entry?;
        if !artist_entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
            continue;
        }
        let artist_dir_path = artist_entry.path();
        let Some(artist_name) = artist_dir_path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) else {
            continue;
        };
        for album_entry in std::fs::read_dir(&artist_dir_path)? {
            let album_entry = album_entry?;
            if !album_entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
                continue;
            }
            let album_dir_path = album_entry.path();
            let Some(album_name) = album_dir_path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) else {
                continue;
            };
            albums.push(StagedAlbum {
                artist_dir_path: artist_dir_path.clone(),
                album_dir_path,
                dir_album: album_name.to_string(),
                identity: resolve_identity(&rows, artist_name, album_name),
            });
        }
    }

    Ok(albums)
}

/// Find the `processed_albums` row a staging directory belongs to. The highest
/// `id` wins when several raw names sanitise to the same two directory names;
/// the ambiguity is warned about, so a shared sanitised name still recovers the
/// most recently tried album.
fn resolve_identity(
    rows: &[crate::db::ProcessedAlbum],
    artist_dir: &str,
    album_dir: &str,
) -> Option<StagedIdentity> {
    let mut matches: Vec<&crate::db::ProcessedAlbum> = rows
        .iter()
        .filter(|row| {
            crate::organizer::sanitize_component(&row.artist).eq_ignore_ascii_case(artist_dir)
                && crate::organizer::sanitize_component(&row.album).eq_ignore_ascii_case(album_dir)
        })
        .collect();
    matches.sort_by_key(|row| row.id);
    let (newest, older) = matches.split_last()?;
    if let Some(first) = older.first() {
        tracing::warn!(
            "Staging {artist_dir:?}/{album_dir:?} matches several processed albums; using the newest {:?} - {:?} (it also matches {:?} - {:?})",
            newest.artist,
            newest.album,
            first.artist,
            first.album
        );
    }
    Some(StagedIdentity {
        artist: newest.artist.clone(),
        album: newest.album.clone(),
        status: newest.status.clone(),
    })
}
```

```rust
/// file was downloaded into a per-disc folder — either a dedicated disc
/// folder ("CD 01", "Disc 2") or an album folder carrying an embedded disc
/// marker ("Gold (Disc 1)"). Walks the parent components and returns the
/// deepest disc folder component. Files flattened directly into the album
/// staging root return `None` so their destination is unchanged.
///
/// `album` is the album title the write is for. The walk stops when a parent
/// directory name equals the sanitised album title, because that names the
/// album staging root: the boundary is the album's own name, not a substring
/// of a flattened slug, so an album whose name contains the separator the old
/// layout used is no longer ambiguous.
///
/// The returned label is the peer's own folder name, so it is run through
/// [`sanitize_component`] before it is handed back: it becomes a real path
/// component in the library, and a peer-supplied name must not reach the
/// filesystem raw.
///
/// Uses [`crate::discs`] so the destination grouping matches the download
/// stager exactly.
fn disc_subdir(src: &Path, album: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let album_component = sanitize_component(album);
    let mut current = src.parent();
    while let Some(dir) = current {
        if let Some(name) = dir.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) {
            // The runner's per-album staging root is <staging>/<artist>/<album>.
            // Its name is the sanitised album title, which can itself carry an
            // embedded "(Disc N)" marker — so it must be recognised before the
            // disc-designator test, never mistaken for one of its own discs.
            if name == album_component {
                break;
            }
            if crate::discs::is_disc_designator(name) {
                // Return the innermost folder, closest to the file. Only the
                // classification is normalized across marker styles; the label
                // itself is the peer's own, so it goes through the sanitiser
                // before it becomes a library path component.
                return Some(sanitize_component(name));
            }
        }
        current = dir.parent();
    }
    None
}
```

```rust
/// Recover interrupted library upgrades by scanning the staging directory for
/// leftover album directories. Directories whose album is marked "success"
/// in the DB are re-verified and copied into the library (crash during the
/// copy step). Every other leftover — an album marked "failed", an album
/// that could not be identified, or a directory whose run never recorded any
/// status — is the debris of an interrupted *download*: the album was never
/// fully staged, so the directory is removed. This keeps a later download
/// for the same album from interleaving with stale `.part` files or partial
/// tracks from the crashed run.
///
/// The identity of each album comes from [`crate::staging::scan`], which
/// matches the sanitised directory names against the raw names the database
/// stores, so a title the sanitiser rewrote is still recovered.
pub fn recover_interrupted_upgrades(
    config: &Config,
    db: &crate::db::Database,
    staging_dir: &Path,
) -> Result<()> {
    if !config.library_upgrade.enabled {
        return Ok(());
    }
    if config.library.paths.is_empty() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let library_root = Path::new(&config.library.paths[0]);

    for staged in crate::staging::scan(staging_dir, db)? {
        let (artist, album) = match &staged.identity {
            Some(identity) => (identity.artist.clone(), identity.album.clone()),
            None => ("Unknown".to_string(), staged.dir_album.clone()),
        };
        match staged.identity.as_ref().map(|identity| identity.status.as_str()) {
            Some("success") => {
                tracing::warn!("Recovering interrupted library upgrade: {artist} - {album}");
                resume_library_upgrade(
                    config,
                    &staged.album_dir_path,
                    library_root,
                    &artist,
                    &album,
                )?;
            }
            // "in-progress" is never written by any code path (downloads
            // record "failed" on interruption), so this arm also covers
            // crashed downloads whose run ended with a recorded failure, a
            // non-success status, or no identity at all.
            _ => {
                tracing::info!(
                    "Cleaning up leftover staging from interrupted run: {artist} - {album}"
                );
                fs::remove_dir_all(&staged.album_dir_path)?;
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
/// Drop a refused album's staged files. A refusal means the set is never
/// written to the library, so keeping it would accumulate unusable audio in
/// `storage.staging_dir` while the album is re-downloaded from scratch on the
/// next run.
///
/// Exactly the paths this run staged are removed, never anything else. Albums
/// are processed concurrently, so the artist directory can hold another album's
/// directory; directories are removed only once they are empty and anything left
/// behind is named in a warning. A directory that was never created is not a
/// failure.
///
/// Ownership is by path, so a foreign file that happens to land on the same path
/// as one of ours is removed with ours — the two are indistinguishable.
fn discard_refused_staging(album_staging: &Path, downloaded: &[PathBuf]) {
    for path in downloaded {
        match std::fs::remove_file(path) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(
                "Failed to remove the staged file {path:?} of a refused download: {e}"
            ),
        }
    }
    match remove_empty_staging_dirs(album_staging) {
        None => {
            if let Some(artist_dir) = album_staging.parent() {
                prune_empty_dir(artist_dir);
            }
        }
        Some(remaining) if remaining == album_staging => tracing::warn!(
            "Leaving {album_staging:?} in place: it could not be removed, and it may hold an entry this run did not stage (leftovers from an earlier run)"
        ),
        Some(remaining) => tracing::warn!(
            "Leaving {album_staging:?} in place: it still holds {remaining:?}, the first entry this run did not stage (a file or subdirectory — leftovers from an earlier run)"
        ),
    }
}

/// Remove a directory once it holds nothing. `remove_dir` refuses a non-empty
/// directory, so a sibling album staged under the same artist is never touched;
/// any failure is a directory that is still in use, which is not an error.
fn prune_empty_dir(dir: &Path) {
    match std::fs::remove_dir(dir) {
        Ok(()) => {}
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
        Err(e) => tracing::debug!("Artist staging dir {dir:?} left in place: {e}"),
    }
}
```

**Step 2 — dependency analysis (this is what determines whether parallelism is real):**

I verified the graph rather than assuming it:

- `src/staging.rs` (new) + `src/lib.rs` are a self-contained foundation; nothing imports `staging::` yet. Independent.
- `src/organizer.rs` Tasks 5-6 depend on `staging::scan` (wave 1). Task 5 (`disc_subdir`) is independent, but Task 6 is not — and both live in the same file, which cannot be split across chunks.
- `src/runner.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `tests/pipeline_test.rs`, `src/download.rs` depend on `staging::album_dir` / `staging::prepare` (wave 1).
- `README.md` + the spec reference check must follow the final code.
- Two waves writing the same working tree in parallel both run `cargo test` in `/data/seakarr`, which contends on `target/` and can compile a half-written sibling file. Parallelism here needs worktree isolation and patch merging — real overhead for effectively one chained change.

So the 7 files are a chain, not a set: **3 sequential waves, one writer at a time.** The sub-agents skill's own rules ("Do NOT dispatch sub-agents for work that has sequential dependencies", "a file belongs to exactly one chunk", "when in doubt, use fewer sub-agents") govern over the file-count table. Agent `implementer` resolves to the builtin `worker` (fresh context, thinking high, edit/write) — confirmed via `list --capabilities`, no substitution needed.

Also: parallel dispatch of two children with identical `model` values is exactly what AGENTS.md critical rule 1 forbids, and in the pi harness `fast` and `implementer` are the same string. Sequential dispatch makes that rule moot.

Each dispatch below is a single child; count of `{ agent:` lines per call = 1.
